newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-LAMAISON SUSPENDED FOR TACKLE ON CHALMERS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LAMAISON SUSPENDED FOR TACKLE ON CHALMERS.

text.p: LONDON, March 23 - French centre Christophe Lamaison was suspended for 30 days on Monday for the tackle which knocked Scotland's Craig Chalmers unconscious during their Five Nations match earlier this month.
Lamaison was handed his punishment by the Five Nations disciplinary committee after being cited for dangerous play by the Scottish Rugby Union.

The Scottish fly-half was left prostrate on the ground after the Brive player's late shoulder charge and had to spend the night in a Paris hospital following the match at the Parc des Prince on March 15.
The incident was missed by referee Ed Morrison but the Scottish authorities decided to take further action after seeing the match video.
Roger Pickering, chief executive of the Five Nations disciplinary commitee said: "Lamaison was given the opportunity to attend the hearing but declined.

"His case was put by French coach Jean Claude Skrela and Guy Laporte, the vice-president of the French federation. The decision to suspend the player was reached after taking into consideration written, oral and video evidence."

Lamaison is the second French international to be suspended this season. Prop Franck Tournaire was banned for one match after stamping on Ireland's replacement hooker Allen Clarke in the Five Nations clash in Dublin.
